# Batch dosing -- OpenPLC starter

*Generated by `tools/gen_starters.py` from the scene's tag set. Do not edit by
hand; regenerate. The program's logic section is yours.*

**The task.** Dose the number of litres on the panel's pot into the tank, then transfer the batch out. Do it with two loops: an inner one that trims pump.speed until meter.rate is the dosing rate you want, and an outer one that watches meter.total and decides what that rate should be — full rate at first, tapering over the last few litres so the cut-off does not carry you past the number. Zero the totaliser before each batch, and remember its reset is a level, not an edge.

**Done when.** The batch lands within a litre or two of the pot, and the tank agrees: 20 L into a 200 L tank is 10 % of level, measured by an instrument that is not the meter. Then halve your dosing rate and run the same recipe — the same litres, in about twice the time. A batch timed in seconds would have delivered half. Finally fail the pump mid-dose (pump.fault) and watch pump.speed hold at whatever you commanded while meter.rate collapses: the flow loop knows within two seconds, and the level will not have moved a whole percent.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| [`batch_dosing.st`](batch_dosing.st) | Every I/O point declared at its located address, with an empty logic section. |
| [`mbconfig.cfg`](mbconfig.cfg) | The Slave Device entry that points OpenPLC's Modbus master at the sidecar. |

The walkthrough for OpenPLC itself -- installing, compiling, timing,
troubleshooting -- is [`docs/OPENPLC.md`](../../../docs/OPENPLC.md). This page
is only what is different about this scene.

## Run it

1. Open the scene in FactoryForge: pick "Batch dosing" on the start screen (or launch with --scene=res://templates/batch_dosing.json).
2. **Then** start the sidecar as the Modbus slave. The order matters: the
   addresses below are the ones it hands out for this scene's tags, and a
   sidecar that was already running when you changed scene keeps its old
   addresses and puts the new tags above them.

   ```bash
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp -o port 5502
   ```

   (From a source checkout: `cd sidecar && python -m factoryforge_sidecar connect ...`.
   If OpenPLC runs in WSL or a VM, add `-o host 0.0.0.0` and read the warning
   it prints.) Check the address map it prints against the table below.
3. Compile `batch_dosing.st` in OpenPLC (web UI *Programs -> Upload*, or copy it
   into `webserver/st_files/` and run `./scripts/compile_program.sh batch_dosing.st`)
   and copy `mbconfig.cfg` to `webserver/core/`,
   or enter these numbers in *Slave Devices -> Add new device*
   (Generic Modbus TCP device, port 5502, slave id 1):

| Block | Start | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Discrete Inputs (%IX100.0) | 0 | 6 |
| Coils (%QX100.0) | 0 | 7 |
| Input Registers (%IW100) | 0 | 10 |
| Holding Registers - Read (%IW100) | 0 | 0 |
| Holding Registers - Write (%QW100) | 0 | 12 |

4. Start the PLC. To have it marked instead, run the grader in place of the
   3D scene -- same tags, same addresses -- and pass the port it prints:

   ```bash
   python tools/grade.py --scene batch-dosing
   factoryforge-sidecar connect --driver modbus-tcp --port <bus port it printed> -o port 5502
   ```

## I/O

`PLC writes` is an output (a motor, a valve, a lamp); `PLC reads` is an input
(a sensor, a button, a measurement). *Brief* marks the signals the task names;
the rest are there to be used, such as each drive's fault contact. Modbus
addresses are decimal, as the sidecar prints them: `0x10` is coil ten.

| Tag | Direction | Type | Modbus | In the program | Meaning | Brief |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `flow_gauge.value` | PLC writes | float | 4x0 + 4x1 | `FlowGaugeValueHi` %QW100 + `FlowGaugeValueLo` %QW101 -> `FlowGaugeValue` : REAL | needle position, scale 0..150 L/min | yes |
| `level_readout.value` | PLC writes | int | 4x2 + 4x3 | `LevelReadoutValueHi` %QW102 + `LevelReadoutValueLo` %QW103 -> `LevelReadoutValue` : DINT | number shown on the display (%) | yes |
| `meter.rate` | PLC reads | float | 3x0 + 3x1 | `MeterRateHi` %IW100 + `MeterRateLo` %IW101 -> `MeterRate` : REAL | measured flow rate, L/min | yes |
| `meter.reset` | PLC writes | bit | 0x0 | `MeterReset` %QX100.0 | a LEVEL: held TRUE keeps the total at zero | yes |
| `meter.total` | PLC reads | int | 3x2 + 3x3 | `MeterTotalHi` %IW102 + `MeterTotalLo` %IW103 -> `MeterTotal` : DINT | litres since the last reset, whole litres | yes |
| `panel.estop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x0 | `PanelEstop` %IX100.0 | E-stop, normally closed: TRUE = healthy, FALSE = pressed; stays pressed until pulled out | yes |
| `panel.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x1 | `PanelGreen` %QX100.1 | green lamp on the panel | yes |
| `panel.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x2 | `PanelRed` %QX100.2 | red lamp on the panel | yes |
| `panel.reset` | PLC reads | bit | 1x1 | `PanelReset` %IX100.1 | Reset button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `panel.setpoint` | PLC reads | float | 3x4 + 3x5 | `PanelSetpointHi` %IW104 + `PanelSetpointLo` %IW105 -> `PanelSetpoint` : REAL | the operator's pot, 5..60 L (starts at 20) | yes |
| `panel.start` | PLC reads | bit | 1x2 | `PanelStart` %IX100.2 | Start button, momentary: a short pulse per press -- latch it | yes |
| `panel.stop` | PLC reads | bit | 1x3 | `PanelStop` %IX100.3 | Stop button, momentary: a short pulse per press | yes |
| `pump.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x4 | `PumpFault` %IX100.4 | motor fault: TRUE = failed; it reports your command and delivers nothing | yes |
| `pump.flow` | PLC reads | float | 3x6 + 3x7 | `PumpFlowHi` %IW106 + `PumpFlowLo` %IW107 -> `PumpFlow` : REAL | measured flow, L/min -- the measurement, not the command | yes |
| `pump.run` | PLC writes | bit | 0x3 | `PumpRun` %QX100.3 | run the pump | yes |
| `pump.speed` | PLC writes | float | 4x4 + 4x5 | `PumpSpeedHi` %QW104 + `PumpSpeedLo` %QW105 -> `PumpSpeed` : REAL | speed reference, 0..100 % | yes |
| `tank.drain` | PLC writes | float | 4x6 + 4x7 | `TankDrainHi` %QW106 + `TankDrainLo` %QW107 -> `TankDrain` : REAL | drain valve opening, 0..100 % | yes |
| `tank.fault` | PLC reads | bit | 1x5 | `TankFault` %IX100.5 | valve fault: TRUE = a valve has seized and holds its opening, whatever you command |  |
| `tank.fill` | PLC writes | float | 4x8 + 4x9 | `TankFillHi` %QW108 + `TankFillLo` %QW109 -> `TankFill` : REAL | fill valve opening, 0..100 % |  |
| `tank.level` | PLC reads | float | 3x8 + 3x9 | `TankLevelHi` %IW108 + `TankLevelLo` %IW109 -> `TankLevel` : REAL | tank level, % of capacity | yes |
| `total_display.value` | PLC writes | int | 4x10 + 4x11 | `TotalDisplayValueHi` %QW110 + `TotalDisplayValueLo` %QW111 -> `TotalDisplayValue` : DINT | number shown on the display (L) | yes |
| `tower.green` | PLC writes | bit | 0x4 | `TowerGreen` %QX100.4 | tower lamp, green |  |
| `tower.red` | PLC writes | bit | 0x5 | `TowerRed` %QX100.5 | tower lamp, red |  |
| `tower.yellow` | PLC writes | bit | 0x6 | `TowerYellow` %QX100.6 | tower lamp, yellow |  |

## Three things this scene's wiring does not forgive

- **A 32-bit value is two registers**, high word first. This scene has 11:
  `flow_gauge.value`, `level_readout.value`, `meter.rate`, `meter.total`,
  `panel.setpoint`, `pump.flow`, `pump.speed`, `tank.drain`, `tank.fill`,
  `tank.level`, `total_display.value`. The program's first and last sections
  move them between the registers and plain DINT/REAL variables, so your logic
  never sees a register. OpenPLC's `DWORD_TO_REAL` converts the *number*
  (`16#3F800000` becomes 1065353216.0, not 1.0), so the starter rebuilds a
  REAL bit by bit instead. [`../check_starters.sh`](../check_starters.sh)
  compiles the helpers with OpenPLC's own matiec and checks them against two
  million bit patterns.
- **Anything polled can be missed if it is short.** OpenPLC's master reads
  every 50 ms. A button click in the 3D scene holds its tag for 0.2 s (the
  panel's Press Hold setting) and then leaves it off for at least as long, so
  every click is read several times: act on its rising edge, not its level.
  The grader holds each press for 0.15 s. The same goes the other way: hold an
  output you want the scene to see for well over one polling period.
- **An output you never write is FALSE.** The master rewrites the whole coil
  block on every poll, including coils your program does not touch.
